parsed.rationale: Although both records are `type-alias-object` kinds with `shared_field_count: 2` and no restraint markers, they carry different names (`PauseWXYC` in `Shared/Intents/Sources/Intents/PauseWXYC.swift` vs. `WhatsPlayingOnWXYC` in `WXYC/iOS/Intents.swift`) that strongly suggest they represent distinct Siri/App Intents actions — one for pausing playback and one for querying what is currently playing. The structural similarity is almost certainly coincidental: both are thin type-alias wrappers over an Intents framework type, so identical shape is expected without the two aliases encoding the same domain concept. Merging or aliasing them to a single name would conflate two semantically separate user-facing intent actions, which would be incorrect.
